title: Acute Chest Pain
clinicalScenario: Adults with acute chest pain requiring immediate triage for ACS and exclusion of life-threatening non-coronary causes.

pathophysiology.summary: Acute coronary syndrome results from acute reduction in coronary blood flow, usually after atheromatous plaque disruption with superimposed thrombosis. Partial or transient occlusion may cause NSTEMI or unstable angina; complete occlusion may cause STEMI. Troponin elevation indicates myocardial injury but is not specific to ACS.

symptoms: Heavy, crushing, or pressure-like retrosternal pain lasting more than 15 minutes
Pain radiating to the arm, neck, jaw, back, or upper abdomen
Diaphoresis, nausea, vomiting, dyspnoea, fatigue, lightheadedness, or syncope
physicalSigns: Hypotension, hypertension, pulmonary oedema, or other signs of acute heart failure
redFlags: ST elevation of at least 1 mm in 2 contiguous leads, new or presumed-new LBBB, or posterior MI pattern
Cardiogenic shock, pulmonary oedema, sustained VT/VF, or high-grade AV block
Abrupt tearing pain, inter-arm blood-pressure difference over 20 mmHg, pulse deficit, or acute neurological deficit
Unilateral absent breath sounds, hyper-resonance, tracheal deviation, or obstructive shock

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Abrupt maximal-onset tearing or stabbing chest/back pain, pulse or blood-pressure asymmetry, neurological deficit, or aortic regurgitation.
Pleuritic pain, sudden dyspnoea, tachycardia, hypoxaemia, or clinical features of DVT.
Sudden pleuritic pain, severe respiratory distress, unilateral reduced breath sounds, hyper-resonance, or tracheal shift.
Burning, meal-related, positional, or reproducible features may support an alternative but do not alone exclude ACS.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: ST elevation, ischemic ST depression, T-wave inversion, new LBBB, or posterior MI pattern.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Acquire and interpret within 10 minutes of first medical contact; repeat when symptoms persist, change, or recur. A normal ECG does not exclude ACS.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Dynamic rise and/or fall with a value above the assay-specific 99th percentile in the clinical context.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Draw at presentation and repeat at 1, 2, or 3 hours according to the validated local assay pathway.

ruleIn.testName: Renal function, electrolytes, glucose, and blood count
ruleIn.modalityTarget: Baseline laboratory assessment — dosing and risk
ruleIn.targetCondition: Renal impairment, electrolyte abnormality, hyperglycaemia, anaemia, or bleeding risk
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Results that alter antithrombin dosing, bleeding-risk assessment, or acute management.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Obtain baseline results before aggressive antithrombotic treatment and interpret them with the local ACS protocol.

ruleOut.targetCondition: Pneumothorax, pulmonary oedema, or other thoracic pathology
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Findings supporting an alternative diagnosis or complication.
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Use when clinically indicated; it does not reliably exclude aortic dissection or ACS.

ruleOut.testName: CT pulmonary angiography or CT aortogram
ruleOut.modalityTarget: Targeted contrast CT — PE or aortic dissection
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Imaging evidence supporting or excluding the suspected emergency.
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Select only when the clinical assessment indicates the relevant life-threatening alternative; do not delay time-critical reperfusion.

clinicalManagement.title: Immediate emergency assessment
actions: Assess airway, breathing, circulation, observations, pain, and haemodynamic or electrical stability.
Obtain and interpret a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of first medical contact and repeat if symptoms persist or evolve.
Establish monitoring and IV access, draw baseline hs-troponin, and assess for aortic dissection, pulmonary embolism, tension pneumothorax, and other life-threatening alternatives.

branches.condition: STEMI, ongoing high-risk ischaemia, shock, acute heart failure, or malignant arrhythmia
actions: Escalate immediately to senior and cardiology teams.
Activate the local reperfusion or resuscitation pathway and arrange transfer to the appropriate capable service.

clinicalManagement.title: STEMI reperfusion pathway
actions: Primary PCI is preferred when the local FMC-to-device target can be met; activate the catheterisation laboratory without delay.
If timely PCI is not available, consider fibrinolysis only when indicated and not contraindicated, followed by transfer to a PCI-capable service.
Administer antiplatelet and parenteral anticoagulant therapy only under the current Saudi/local ACS protocol and after contraindication review.

clinicalManagement.title: NSTE-ACS risk stratification and angiography
actions: Use serial ECG, serial hs-troponin, renal function, bleeding risk, and a validated risk pathway.
Immediate invasive assessment is required for refractory angina, haemodynamic instability, acute heart failure, or life-threatening arrhythmia.
Consider early invasive assessment for high-risk features such as dynamic ST-T changes, elevated hs-troponin, or high GRACE risk.
Use selective non-invasive testing only after validated low-risk assessment and exclusion of life-threatening alternatives.

clinicalManagement.title: Low-risk chest pain rule-out and safety net
actions: Consider early discharge only after a validated rapid hs-troponin pathway, low HEART score, non-dynamic ECG, and clinical exclusion of life-threatening non-coronary causes.
Provide explicit return precautions and arrange timely cardiology or rapid-access chest-pain follow-up.

medicationPlan.note: UNREVIEWED DRAFT — NOT FOR CLINICAL USE. The supplied blueprint contains exact aspirin, GTN, opioid, P2Y12, and heparin doses. Those claims must be reconciled against the applicable Saudi/local ACS protocol, product labelling, contraindications, renal function, bleeding risk, reperfusion strategy, and reviewer metadata before any medication regimen is added or approved.

patientEducation: Explain that possible ACS requires urgent assessment even if pain improves.
Call emergency services immediately if chest pain recurs, radiates to the arm or jaw, or is accompanied by sweating or breathlessness.
lifestyleAndDiet: After stabilisation, address smoking, diet, activity, lipid risk, and adherence to secondary prevention.
mdtReferrals: Pharmacy and primary care for medication and risk-factor follow-up
dischargeCriteria: No ongoing instability or unresolved high-risk feature
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: For confirmed ACS, arrange cardiology follow-up and cardiac rehabilitation as appropriate. For low-risk discharge, arrange rapid-access chest-pain or primary-care follow-up within the locally approved timeframe.
